s1.syndrome_frame: Bilateral vision loss with uveitis and retinitis in an immunocompromised patient
salient_findings: Low CD4 count and high HIV RNA level
Pruritic back rash with crusting erythematous plaques
Uveitis and retinitis with vitreous haze and retinal whitening
key_facts: Patient has HIV and is not receiving antiretroviral therapy
CD4 count is 24 cells/mm3
HIV RNA level is 175,000 copies/mL
Patient has multiple sexual partners with inconsistent protection
Patient presents with bilateral photophobia and decreased vision
Uncorrected visual acuity is hand motions in both eyes
Intraocular pressures are 14 and 9 mm Hg in the right and left eye, respectively
Aqueous fluid from both eyes is negative for herpetic viral DNA by PCR
Vitreous cultures are negative for bacteria and fungi
Cerebrospinal fluid is negative for VDRL and other microbiologic studies
Rapid plasma reagin testing shows a 1:64 titer
Cerebrospinal fluid T pallidum particle agglutiation assay is positive
Skin lesion histopathology shows interface dermatitis with spirochetes

shortlist.label: Syphilitic uveitis
shortlist.why_kept: Positive cerebrospinal fluid T pallidum particle agglutination assay and skin lesion histopathology showing interface dermatitis with spirochetes

shortlist.label: Cytomegalovirus retinitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient has HIV with low CD4 count and high HIV RNA level, making CMV retinitis a likely opportunistic infection

shortlist.label: Toxoplasmosis
shortlist.why_kept: Common opportunistic infection in immunocompromised patients, particularly those with HIV

shortlist.label: Syphilitic retinitis
shortlist.why_kept: Clinical presentation and positive syphilis testing suggest syphilitic involvement of the retina

shortlist.label: Progressive outer retinal necrosis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient's immunocompromised state and clinical presentation of bilateral vision loss with retinitis

raw.rationale: The patient's positive cerebrospinal fluid T pallidum particle agglutination assay and rapid plasma reagin testing with a 1:64 titer, along with the skin lesion histopathology showing interface dermatitis with spirochetes, strongly suggest syphilis infection. The ocular findings of bilateral photophobia, decreased vision, and intraocular inflammation are consistent with syphilitic uveitis, especially in the context of a patient with HIV and a low CD4 count.

rejected.label: Cytomegalovirus retinitis
rejected.why: Aqueous fluid from both eyes was negative for herpetic viral DNA by PCR, which makes CMV retinitis less likely

rejected.label: Toxoplasmosis
rejected.why: There is no specific evidence of Toxoplasma gondii infection in the provided case facts

rejected.label: Syphilitic retinitis
rejected.why: While the patient has syphilis, the primary ocular finding is uveitis rather than retinitis

rejected.label: Progressive outer retinal necrosis
rejected.why: The clinical presentation and laboratory findings do not specifically support this diagnosis
